builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Rek'Sai: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (1,490 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 57.7% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A tunnel-based melee ambusher who uses burrowed tracking to choose an entry, then spends Fury on a bite or recovery. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Titanic Hydra → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Plated Steelcaps, Guardian Angel, Sterak's Gage.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Titanic Hydra → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Titanic Hydra → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 57.7% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Titanic Hydra → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

builds.name: Fury entry barrage
builds.summary: Reach finite Fury quickly after unburrowing and reserve it for E.
builds.goal: Reach finite Fury quickly after unburrowing and reserve it for E.
builds.hypothesis: Passive grants 25 Fury per attack or ability; unburrowed Q empowers three attacks with 35% speed. E calculations list an AD term and 1.2 empowered multiplier despite unresolved cross-reference rendering. BotRK and a finite Hullbreaker fifth-hit state support actual attacks, while Stridebreaker maintains contact; primary R resets W.
testPlan: Required state: Enter with stated Fury and log each ability/attack before choosing E.
Record Fury after every action and E damage type at submax versus max Fury; compare R's W reset.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Burrowing spends Fury on healing or crowd control prevents the Q sequence.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: An unresolved E tooltip cross-reference is not absent data: the calculation exists, but its raw AD flag still needs verification. Titanic cannot be combined with Stridebreaker; choose one Cleave item.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Blade of The Ruined King, Hullbreaker, Stridebreaker, Sterak's Gage, Death's Dance, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.

builds.name: Burrow recovery cycle
builds.summary: Trade a burst window for a safe three-second burrow heal and reentry.
builds.goal: Trade a burst window for a safe three-second burrow heal and reentry.
builds.hypothesis: Passive consumes Fury over three seconds to restore a health-based amount. Visage and health purchases test the recovery value; Cleaver's physical ramp benefits Q attacks before retreat. Tunnel entrances give a planned exit, subject to per-tunnel reuse limits.
testPlan: Required state: Fury earned in combat, protected tunnel exit and sufficient time to finish recovery.
Measure actual burrow recovery at matched Fury/health with and without Visage, and time to reentry.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Pursuit denies healing time or insufficient bonus health leaves Warmog inactive.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Tunnels do not remove their own reuse cooldowns or allow attacks while burrowed.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
